newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ business confidence negative in May - Nat Bank.
newsitem.headline: NZ business confidence negative in May - Nat Bank.

text.p: New Zealand Business confidence was negative for the second month running, with a net eight percent of respondents anticipating a deterioration in business conditions over the next 12 months, the National Bank said in its May survey released on Friday.
This compared with six percent in April, which -- barring the pre-election period last year -- was the lowest confidence has reached in six years.
The bank said in its monthly survey the gloom was spread across all sectors, except for services which was only mildly optimistic.
Respondents were also generally negative about their own activity outlooks, and less upbeat about investment, employment, unemployment and profits.
In line with recent data showing a slowing economy, inflation was expected to hit 2.6 percent, from 2.7 percent in the April survey.

Only a net three percent of respondents intended to raise prices in the short term. The survey said the Reserve Bank would be pleased the inflationary construction sector expected to hold prices steady over the next three months.
Interest rate expectations eased in light of emerging excess capacity, with 11 percent picking rates to decline. This contrasted with 26 percent last month anticipating a rise.
"This volatility in expectations highlights the precarious stage of the business cycle," National Bank said. "A turning point is near, but the upswing appears another quarter or so away."
Just a net 23 percent of respondents foresaw a rise in exports, a level around the lows over the past 10 years.
Only a net 1.4 percent expect profits to rise. Construction, agriculture and retail overwhelmed mild optimism in manufacturing and slightly improved profit optimism in services.
